Additionally, as AI technologies, policies, and the roles of individuals within and outside the AI governance committee continuously evolve, ongoing education and training for committee members will enable adaptation to these changes and promote a common understanding among members.

unlisted_practices: Appoint an executive sponsor, positioned one level below the CEO, to own, drive, and coordinate AI governance committee activities and report to senior leadership.
Regularly update AI governance committee membership to rotate expertise and avoid concentrating control over AI use in a small group.
Staff the AI governance committee with clinical, technical, social, informatics, operational, and ethics and legal expertise, structured into specialized subcommittees.
Define key measures of success and specific metrics for evaluating the effectiveness of AI governance.
Actively seek input from patient community members to build a transparent system that shares information about AI solutions with patients and community stakeholders.
Define ownership and operational responsibilities and document ownership for technical capabilities and infrastructure across the AI product lifecycle.
Allocate costs for AI technical infrastructure and provide baseline functionality such as data analysis, model monitoring, and outcome evaluation from IT to departments as a complimentary service.
Assess organizational AI governance readiness by evaluating existing capabilities and gaps across people, process, technology, and operations domains.
